export.readme.premiere.title: {title}, {cut} – import into Premiere Pro
export.readme.where: These files belong in the folder {folder} (the subfolder _cutlery of your footage folder). The timeline finds your original clips, the music, the titles and the maps from there.
export.readme.premiere.steps:
1. In Premiere Pro: File → Import, choose {timeline}. A new sequence appears in the project.
2. If clips appear offline: right-click → Link Media, select the first missing clip in your footage folder; Premiere finds the others.
3. Subtitles: File → Import, choose {srt}, drag it onto the sequence as a caption track.
4. Titles are PNG pictures on their own video track; replace them with your own titles if you like.
5. Render the film from the sequence (File → Export → Media).

export.readme.fcp.title: {title}, {cut} – import into Final Cut Pro
export.readme.fcp.steps:
1. In Final Cut Pro: File → Import → XML…, choose {timeline}. A new event with the project appears in the library.
2. If clips appear offline: select them, File → Relink Files → Original Media, and choose your footage folder.
3. Subtitles are in the timeline as captions; {srt} is there in case you need it elsewhere.
4. Titles are PNG pictures on a connected lane; replace them with your own titles if you like.
5. Stabilisation is switched on for the shots that need it; Final Cut analyses them after the import.
6. Share the film from the project (File → Share).
export.readme.fcp.not_included: Not included and marked instead (markers on the clips): high-pass, speech enhancement and compressor of single shots, and the decisions from the review.
export.readme.resolve.title: {title}, {cut} – import into DaVinci Resolve
export.readme.resolve.steps:
1. In DaVinci Resolve: File → Import → Timeline…, choose {timeline}. Leave “Automatically import source clips into media pool” switched on.
2. If clips appear offline: select them in the media pool, right-click → Relink Selected Clips…, and choose your footage folder.
3. Subtitles: if the timeline has no subtitle track, File → Import → Subtitle…, choose {srt} and drag it onto the timeline.
4. Titles are PNG pictures on their own video track; replace them with your own titles if you like.
5. Render the film on the Deliver page.
export.readme.resolve.not_included: Not included and marked instead (markers on the clips): stabilisation and audio cleanup of single shots, and the decisions from the review.
export.readme.filmcraft.title: {title}, {cut} – open in FilmCraft
export.readme.filmcraft.steps:
1. Open {timeline} in FilmCraft (File → Open). It is the project you saw in the review: titles, map, music, levels, stabilisation and subtitles are in it.
2. The project refers to your original clips and to the music in this folder. If FilmCraft reports missing media: Relink Media, choose the first missing clip in your footage folder; FilmCraft finds the others.
3. {srt} is there in case you need the subtitles elsewhere.
4. Export the film from FilmCraft.
export.readme.filmcraft.not_included: Everything from the review is included.
export.readme.premiere.not_included: Not included and marked instead (markers on the sequence): stabilisation and audio cleanup of single shots, and the decisions from the review.
